November 2009 





## Global Recovery is Underway 



- Our initial estimates for Q3 show that the modest improvement in the market that began to show in Q2 has continued, and as a result we can say that at a global level the recovery in the copper wirerod and wire and cable markets is now underway. This recovery is at present weak and patchy and is very much led by China with some help from India and South Korea, with little sign of any significant upturn yet in the European and North American markets. In North East Asia the Japanese and Taiwanese markets also remain depressed. 



- Overall our data shows that for the first three quarters of 2009 global copper wirerod consumption fell by 10.0% year-on-year. As we have now passed the anniversary of the start of the global economic crisis hitting, Q4 year-on-year comparisons will look much better. We are currently expecting that there will only be a small fall in copper wirerod consumption compared to Q4 2008, and there is even the possibility of a return to growth. 



- Despite the improving economic outlook, with the likelihood of a double dip recession receding, the road to recovery across the whole cable industry in terms of both geography and product and market sectors will be a slow one, with some product sectors yet to feel the full impact. As a result the effects of this recession will continue to be felt by the wirerod and wire and cable industries for a number of years.

© 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 12 November 2009 Copper wire, cable and wirerod **www.crugroup.com** # Europe Our numbers indicate that copper wirerod production in Europe totalled 715,000t in Q3, down by 18% y- o-y. Wire and cable production amounted to 548,000t, which was a 22% y-o-y contraction. Southern Europe continues to be challenged by sluggish demand and the ongoing credit squeeze. More positive sentiment is experienced in some of the major Northern European markets. ### **Spain remains deep in recession** After the termination of the **Prysmian/Draka** merger talks, Prysmian reported that it has €1.0bn (US$1.5bn) in liquidity to finance growth projects. It is to target acquisitions in high-growth potential regions such as Russia, India and China. It was reported that some deals could be closed by the end of this year. Meanwhile, German exports of wirerod and drawn wire fell to 102,000t in Q3, a 17% y-o-y contraction. However, from a q-o-q point of view, the number rose 18% sequentially, providing encouraging signs for W. Europe’s largest exporter. When **General Cable** announced its Q3 financial results, it reported that sales volumes in Europe and North Africa plunged by 28% y-o-y in Q3 whilst those in the nine months to September declined by 17%. General Cable has seen its market in Iberia fall by almost 50%. This is primarily attributed to the severe slowdown in the Spanish construction sector after a decade of exceptionally strong growth. We estimate that total shipments of copper wire and cable in Spain plunged by 47% y-o-y to 29,000t in Q3, which was 48% lower than in Q2, indicating that the Spanish market remains deep in recession. This sequential contraction in Q3 is also exhibited in the consumption of copper wirerod and drawn wire which dived by 48% q-o-q to 33,000t. In the same period, German consumption of copper wirerod and drawn wire increased by 5% q-o-q to 121,000t. ### **Case study: Nexans** **Nexans** published its Q3 sales figures and announced that it experienced a 19% organic shrinkage. For the nine months to September the decrease was 17% whilst H1 declined by 16%. The deteriorating performance is attributed to lower building cable sales in Europe and Asia-Pacific and setbacks in the execution of high-voltage contracts. Energy cable revenues in Q3 were down by 13% y-o-y. Deliveries of low and medium voltage cables to the major European markets in Q3 remained unchanged with the exception of Italy and Greece. Automotive harnesses saw sequential improvement in Q3, with late June ha

ving been the bottom. Building cable sales in Europe continued to be challenging. Shipments of telecom cables in Q3 plunged by 19%. In line with planned cutbacks in production capacity, electrical wire sales in Q3 were down by 35%. Nexans commented that Europe is characterised by overcapacity in electrical wires; demand is insufficient while medium term prospects remain poor. Further to the announcement of the company’s plans to close its **Chauny** copper wirerod and wire plant, a strike started in mid-September. The wirerod output lost is now being supplied by **Aurubis** who already sells material to Nexans. Aurubis has reportedly agreed to sell several thousand tonnes of additional copper wirerod until the end of the year. The Chauny plant had an annual capacity of 290,000t of copper wirerod and 49,000t of copper wire. The remaining copper wirerod mills of Nexans in France and Germany have a combined output capacity of 220,000t per annum. |Cable only|||||||||||| |Data: CRU||||||||||||| © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 5 of 12 November 2009 Copper wire, cable and wirerod **www.crugroup.com** # North America ### **Third quarter was still weak but looks to have stabilised** As expected, the North American wire and cable market did not pick up from Q2 remaining essentially flat. Wire and cable output fell by 22% y-o-y while demand declined 23% y-o-y for the third quarter this year. The decline in copper wirerod production in Canada was the most severe within the region, with volumes dropping by 31% y-o-y in Q3, largely due to low exports to the US and also a consistent decline in domestic wire and cable consumption. **Nexans** signed an agreement to sell its Montreal rod mill to AmRod but the deal was terminated in September, as **AmRod** did not meet the conditions in the agreement. Wirerod output in Canada is therefore set to fall sharply next year when the plant is likely to cease operation if no buyer can be found. Nevertheless, the downturn in the US is still leading the regional downward trend for the first nine months of the year, w

ith volumes falling by almost 25% y-o-y. In Q3, total regional energy cable output fell by 22% y-o-y and 2% on Q2. Winding wire was down 25% y-o-y and 4% on Q2 while communication cable was down 18% y-o-y and 4% on Q2. However, the sequential falls were much lower than in Q1 to Q2 which is further evidence that the bottom has been reached. **General Cable** reported Q3 volumes down 21% y-o-y. **Encore Wire** said Q3 unit volume decreased 9% on Q2 as the slowdown in construction has created a volatile pricing environment that has narrowed the gap between raw material costs and sale prices. **CommScope** also reported lower sales volumes, with sales still declining in most products except the Enterprise and Broadband segments that saw sequential improvement during the third quarter. ### **Outlook for the remainder of the year still poor** US housing starts in September totalled 590,000 at a seasonal adjusted rate, 7% lower than the same month a year ago. Residential construction spending in August increased by 4% m-o-m but was down 26% y-o-y. The level of building activity is still weak but has seen the bottom, according to market participants. However, it is unlikely to improve significantly due to low demand driven by unemployment which was still on the rise in September. Non-residential construction spending continued to drop, by 0.4% m-o-m and 5% y-o-y in August, with commercial spending shrinking by 33% y-o-y (mostly in the private sector). This remains one of the biggest concerns for wire and cable manufacturers, who believe low offtake from this sector next year will drag any improvement backward. We totally agree with this view and do not foresee any recovery until next year, particularly as credit remains a major problem for small businesses. Vehicle production utilisation is forecast to improve y-o-y in November, according to Ward’s Auto. With demand staying flat, the y-o-y comparison should be favourable in Q4. ### **New capacity for Prysmian and Sarkuysan in the USA** In October, Italian cable manufacturer **Prysmian** opened its first extra high voltage (EHV), vertical continuous vulcanization (VCV) power cable plant in North America, located in Abbeville, SC. Meanwhile, **Sarkuysan** said that its new plant in Albany, NY, will produce around 12,000 tonnes of copper wire annually and will produce at full capacity starting from November. e latest data from the **Japanese Cable Makers’ Association** (JCMA) shows that copper wire and cable shipments fell by 17.4% year-onyear in September. This compares to a year-on-year fall of 17.7% in August. Demand from the automotive sector remains low with automobile production in September 21.6% down on August 2008. This is the 12<sup>th</sup> consecutive month of lower year-on-year vehicle production. The fall in demand for automotive wire is further impacted by the greater decline in production of larger, more cable intensive vehicles. Production of passenger cars over 2000 cc fell by 25.2% in September compared to a fall of 13.1% in small car output. The construction sector continues to be depressed as a result of tighter building regulations and low levels of investment, and no quick recovery is forecast. 

Although there are some modest signs of an improvement in the market, any recovery is at best very slow and as a result the JCMA has revised downwards its forecast for metallic cable demand for this financial year ending in March 2010. It now expects consumption of 648,000 tonnes conductor, which is 14.6% down on the previous financial year. This compares to an earlier forecast of 705,000 tonnes. This will be the first time the market has fallen below 700,000 tonnes since 1974. The downward revision has been across all the main product sectors. In the first three quarters of 2009 we estimate that copper cable production fell by 22.4% year-on-year, with copper wirerod output down by 25.0%. 

### **South Korea is the one bright spot in the region** 

The performance of the South Korean market continues to exceed expectations, with the South Korean economy growing at its fastest rate since Q1 2002 in Q3 2009. GDP increased by 2.9% compared to Q2 2009 and was 0.6% up year-on-year. The manufacturing sector grew by 8.7% compared to Q2, driven by increased output of cars and also electronic products. For 2009 as a whole GDP is forecast to fall by just 0.8% with industrial production only 2.2% lower. The construction sector is staging a modest recovery with growth of 1.1% year-on-year in the period Q1 to Q3 this year compared to a fall of 2.4% in the whole of 2008. The improving economic outlook is reflected in growing consumer confidence with the Composite Consumer Sentiment Index (CCSI) rising by 3 points in October to 117. This compares with a level of just 84 in March this year. As a result of both stronger home demand and increased exports we estimate that Korean copper wirerod production grew by 7.1% in the first three quarters of this year, with copper cable production falling by just 2.0%. 

### **Taiwanese market still over 20% down** 

The Taiwanese wire and cable market is continuing to struggle, although starting in August there has been some signs of a modest improvement in production. For the first eight months of 2008 winding wire production was down by 36% with electronic wire output 40% lower. Overall we estimate that copper w

e production and further analysis on the use of scrap in the production of copper wirerod in China. This has led us to believe that there was greater production of wirerod in China in 2008 from scrap, and as a result we have upped our estimates for copper wirerod consumption in 2008 to 4,075,000 t from 3,708,000t. For Q1-Q3 of 2009 we estimate that copper wirerod production grew by 9.0% compared to 2008, with consumption rising by 7.0%. Local demand for wire and cable continues to be boosted by Government stimulus measures which are more than making up for any reduction in demand from goods made for export. Investment in infrastructure, including spending on expansion of the electricity grid and railway network, plus the building of new airports and low cost housing, is helping demand of energy cables, whilst the market for winding wire is being boosted by incentives to buy new domestic appliances. The continuing surge in vehicle production, with output up by 31.7% year-on-year in the first three quarters of 2009, is helping both the energy and winding wire sectors. It’s not all good news though with external copper telecom cable demand down by around 40% this year, and demand for shipwiring cable heading lower as orders for new ships dry up. Meanwhile the fall in electricity consumption at the start of this year has resulted in a slowdown in growth for electricity generation equipment including large transformers. 

GDP year-on-year growth has accelerated in Q3 to 8.9%, and our full year forecast is now for an 8.2% increase. The construction sector is one of the main elements driving this rising growth with floor space completed rising by 32% in the quarter. Industrial production is also increasing and is expected to be up in the range of 15%-20% in Q4 of this year. However, there are some clouds on the horizon as inflation is starting to rise. With lending continuing to increase there is a significant risk of asset price inflation, and as a result policy tightening is expected to begin in Q1 2010. This will then test how resilient the current recovery is, as the stimulus measures begin to be unwound. 

### **North Africa has good growth potential** 

Production and consumption of copper wire and cable in North Africa has held up quite well so far in 2009, and there is good potential for further growth. This will make the countries of Morocco, Tunisia, Algeria and Libya attractive for exporters of both copper wirerod and also wire and cable. Imports of copper wirerod into these four countries grew by 8.2% in the first half of 2009 compared to H1 2008, with almost all of this rod coming from Europe, primarily Belgium, Germany, Italy and Spain. Local wire and cable demand remains good, whilst the slump in consumption of automotive harnesses in Western Europe is being largely offset by the ongoing migration of harness production from Eastern Europe to Tunisia and Morocco. © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 11 of 12 November 2009 Copper wire, cable and wirerod **www.crugroup.com** # Industry News Chinese copper wirerod producer **TCICO** has commissioned its second Contirod plant which has an annual capacity of 150,000 tpy. This plant is close to the company’s first line, commissioned in 2001. Turkish winding wire manufacturer **Elsan Elektrik Gerecieri SA** has placed an order for a Rautomead RS3000/6 copper rod casting machine with a nominal capacity of 6,000 tpy. Egypt’s **El Sewedy Cables** has begun production of power cables at its new 10,000 conductor tpy capacity plant in Ethiopia. El Sewedy has an 85.7% share of the company with the balance held by local partner **Dynamic General Trading** . China’s **Jangxi Rare Earth and Rare Metals Tungsten Group Corp.** is to install a new 120,000 tpy copper rod plant using Properzi-La Farga technology that enables scrap to be directly refined. **Nexans** is to close its 300,000 tpy rod plant at Chauny, but may increase production at its two remaining plants at Lens in France and Bramsche in Germany. Staff at Chauny have been on strike since the announcement was made.
